subject: MSA/OrderForm discussion: downstream productization, training opt-out, and telemetry
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@acme.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft redlines (Order Form + MSA) — output/use questions

Sean — attaching our consolidated redlines for the Order Form and the MSA. Our legal team flagged several items where Acme wants to preserve downstream productization rights and ensure we have clarity on training/telemetry. High-level asks from our side: 

- We need a clear carve-in that allows Acme to bundle outputs into our customer-facing product (i.e., downstream productization).
- We require an explicit affirmative license to use outputs internally and to distribute them to our customers.
- We want an opt-out mechanism for any training/feedback collection if certain datasets are sensitive; ideally this is an Order Form checkbox per environment.
- Telemetry/usage metrics: we need a guarantee that Redwood will not surface PII in aggregated telemetry reports; redlines propose stricter anonymization.

Attached: ACME_OrderForm_redline_v3.docx and a short redline_summary.pdf. Can your team confirm which of these are deal-breakers for Redwood and propose alternative language where necessary? We need to finalize for procurement approval by next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Head of Product Contracts, Acme Corporation

Marta — thanks for the redlines and clear summary. Appreciate the timeline; we can be aligned for procurement next Wednesday but need to triage a few items now so we can surface proper legal/ops trade-offs. Quick responses to your bullets below; detailed suggested language will follow from Laura.

1) Downstream productization: We generally permit Customers to use outputs in their products, but we protect our models and training IP. Typical approach: customer gets a non-exclusive right to use and distribute outputs produced by the Service, provided they do not claim ownership of our models or attempt to retrain/redistribute model weights. Is Acme comfortable with a clause that distinguishes "output" from "model" and restricts "retraining" to explicit separate licensing?

2) Affirmative license for distribution: Agree in principle. We'll propose a focused Order Form section that grants distribution rights for outputs, scoped to the Customer's business units and with a prohibitive clause on redistributing to third-party model builders.

3) Training opt-out per environment: We can support an opt-out checkbox on the Order Form to disable Redwood feedback collection and model-improvement use for specific deployments/environments. Operational note: opt-out can increase unit costs and affect latency/quality improvements; we'll call that out. We can include an SLA adjustment if opt-out is enabled (reduces caching/aggregation benefits).

4) Telemetry/PII: We already anonymize telemetry but will take your redline seriously. Laura — can you propose tightened anonymization language and an attestation for PII handling? Monica can scope the operational burden and flag any perf/cost implications.

Next steps: Laura will send proposed clause wording (MSA/Order Form) and a short memo on operational impact. Ben — please prepare a short note on pricing delta if Acme opts out of feedback/training. Marta — if possible, highlight which of the proposed redlines are "must-haves" vs "nice-to-haves" so we can prioritize.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher

Subject: Proposed language for output, training opt-out, and telemetry

Team / Marta — below is draft clause language I recommend we propose back to Acme. I focused on clear delineation between "Output" and "Model", a per-environment opt-out mechanism for training/feedback, and tightened telemetry assurances. Laura's comments in-line where we may need commercial concessions.

1) Output vs Model (MSA, Section X.Y - Proposed):
"Customer Data" and "Customer Outputs": For clarity, "Customer Outputs" means text, code, images or other artifacts generated by the Service in response to Customer Data. Subject to Customer's payment and compliance with the Agreement, Redwood grants Customer a worldwide, non-exclusive, transferable (to Customer's affiliates), sublicensable limited license to use, reproduce, modify, and distribute Customer Outputs as part of Customer's products and services. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer acknowledges that Redwood retains all rights, title, and interest in and to the underlying model weights, architectures, training datasets, and any model improvements made by Redwood (collectively, "Redwood Models"). Customer shall not reverse engineer, decompile, export, or attempt to extract model weights or replicate Redwood Models without a separate commercial license.

Comment: This mirrors standard market language. Acme's redline pushes for broader ownership — we should hold firm on model ownership.

2) Training / Feedback Opt-out (Order Form Addendum):
"Training Opt-Out": Customer may elect, via a checkbox on the Order Form or via a documented API flag for particular environments, to opt-out of Redwood's use of Customer Data and Customer Outputs for the purpose of training, improving, or benchmarking Redwood Models. If Customer elects the "Opt-Out", Redwood will not include Customer Data in its model training datasets or use it to improve general models. Opt-Out Impacts: (a) Redwood may disable certain caching/aggregation optimizations, which could measurably increase per-token cost; (b) certain quality improvements will not be applied to the Customer's instances; and (c) incident triage that relies on aggregated telemetry may be delayed. Parties agree to negotiate a reasonable adjustment to fees if Opt-Out is selected.

Comment: We can accept opt-outs limited to Customer Data/Outputs but avoid blanket prohibitions that would prevent Redwood from using anonymized, aggregated usage signals for product improvements. We should also reserve the right to use anonymized telemetry (see next).

3) Telemetry & PII Safeguards (Order Form / Security Appendix):
"Telemetry": Redwood will collect operational telemetry and aggregated usage metrics necessary for performance, security, and product improvement. Redwood will not disclose Customer Data, Customer Outputs, or any PII in telemetry reports. Redwood will (i) apply industry-standard anonymization; (ii) provide an attestation on request demonstrating PII handling practices; and (iii) offer an additional contractual commitment to delete raw telemetry associated with Customer Data on contract termination, subject to lawful retention requirements.

Comment: If Acme requires cryptographic proofs or specific KMS/HSM treatments for telemetry artifacts, that typically sits in an Enterprise SOW and may carry add-on fees.

Attachments: I drafted a short plain-text "proposed_clause_markdown.txt" with the exact language for insertion in the next redline. Please review and let me know which pieces we want to concede. Ben — can you estimate a per-month delta for Opt-Out for 3 tiers: small (dev), medium (staging), large (prod)? Monica — can you document any operational changes needed to support per-environment switches (timeline & runbook).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Sean / Laura / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear proposed language. Acme's legal reviewed Laura's wording and we can accept the proposed Output vs Model distinction with the following small edits: 

- Please add the phrase "including derivative works" after the definition of "Customer Outputs" so it is explicit that we can create derived catalogs for our customers.
- For the Opt-Out Impacts, we need the fee adjustment to be a defined % range rather than an open-ended negotiation; propose 10-25% uplift per environment depending on traffic class.
- Telemetry attestation: agree, but we need Redwood to provide the initial attestation and PII-handling summary as part of the negotiated package (attachment to Order Form).

If Redwood can accept those edits, Acme is happy to move to counter-signature and DocuSign routing. We view the opt-out as a material requirement for a subset of our customers with regulated data.

I'll mark the three items above as "must-have". Rest are "nice-to-have." Once you confirm, we'll route to procurement and get the countersigned Order Form processed.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Head of Product Contracts, Acme Corporation
